Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: LSR greets freshers with music, memories and monsoon showers
Article Text:
Freshers explore the campus on their first day at LSR on Tuesday

Prof. Kanika K Ahuja, principal of LSR shared short inspirational stories for students and explained what the magic of LSR is like

The magic of LSR is real: Principal

Energetic performances by the music and dance societies of LSR added a festive spirit to the day

Nostalgic energy for alumni

(L-R) Chef Gauri Varma, batch of 2004, Principal Kanika K Ahuja, Mugdha Sinha, batch of 1995





Welcoming freshers with thunder and rain, Delhi University opened its doors for the new session on Tuesday. As students entered wide-eyed and bushy-tailed, Lady Shri Ram College for Women celebrated womanhood and equal opportunity. The packed hall was filled with vibrant musical energy as the college song played, which was written by alumna Smita Vats and set to music by alumna Janaki Ganesh under the guidance of Pandit Viswamohan Bhatt. Energetic performances by the music and dance societies of LSR added a festive spirit to the day. The stage came alive with the fusion of classical, Indian, and Western music.A hoarding outside the front gate read “We don’t break glass ceilings, we’re building a new floor”. Prof. Kanika K Ahuja, principal of LSR shared short inspirational stories for students and explained what the magic of LSR is like. "Some of you will feel nervous, a little intimidated. Relax because at LSR we don't rush you to bloom. We help you blow your roots first. Your teachers, your mentors, your seniors, your societies, that's your soil. And one day, you will be the shade for somebody else. They say there is magic here at LSR.You'll hear this phrase very often, and I hope you experience the magic because it's real.” The acronyms for LSR’s values guide the students: Leadership with Social Responsibility, Lakshya, Sadhana, and Rachna, were interwoven in her address to students.An IAS officer Mugdha Sinha, batch of 1995 and Chef Gauri Varma, batch of 2004 were guests of honour who shared anecdotes from their time at the college. Mugdha Sinha shared her favourite memories and relatable incidents for students. “It’s an honour and privilege to be here today. It took me 34 years to move from where you’re sitting to this stage. I stand here with a lot of nostalgia and warm memories. While the principal addressed you, I thought it was my reorientation as well to see the change that has come about in LSR in the past three decades,” she said.Talking about how teachers allowed students to be their authentic self, Gauri Varma recalled an anecdote from her time as a B.Com student. “I forgot there was a test and I didn’t know anything that I could write. Instead of leaving the pages blank, I wrote a live play-by-play of what was happening in class at that time. And I handed it in. My teacher did nothing. That is what LSR does, it lets you be you. I thought that I got away with it but now I realise what she did.”
Article Summary: Lady Shri Ram College for Women opened its doors for the new session on Tuesday. An IAS officer Mugdha Sinha, batch of 1995 and Chef Gauri Varma,batch of 2004 were guests of honour. Prof. Kanika K Ahuja, principal of LSR shared inspirational stories for students.

Article Title: Latika Katt's final works find a home
Article Text:
Latika Katt's works are displayed at the Gallery Threshold in Sarvodaya Enclave

Curator of the exhibition Tunty Chauhan with Anya Singh

Latika Katt worked with a wide range of materials, including bronze, stone, and marble

Muzaffar and Meera Ali

'Her works had architectural sensibility'

Latika often named nature and the city of Varanasi as her constant influences, with decay and duration being her lifelong subjects

Aman Nath

Nilima Shaikh and Jatin Das





Walk into the gallery in a Sarvodaya Enclave home, and you enter the final chapter of sculptor Latika Katt's artistic journey. The exhibition at Gallery Threshold brings together Abandoned, the last series she created before her passing in January last year.A suspended metallic work greets visitors at the entrance, while 13 bronze-and-stone sculptures from the series occupy the floor. On the walls are delicate graphite drawings that reveal the artist's quieter, meditative side. "The idea was to represent her in totality. You see the softness of her graphite drawings and then the strength of the materials she worked with. Both sides of her personality are present here," said curator Tunty Chauhan, who decided on doing an exhibition of the sculptor's works about two years ago.A six-minute short film by filmmaker Muzaffar Ali, screened at the preview, featured Katt and her lifelong inspiration, Varanasi, where she was born. Remembering Katt, he said, "She was intensely passionate about her work. When I saw her sculpture based on the ghats of Varanasi, I felt they were designed to receive light in different ways. Her works weren't just sculptural; they had an architectural sensibility.I wanted to film more of her while she was making sculptures, woh reh gaya."Aman Nath, a close friend of Katt and who attended the preview, recalled that the two had planned a sculpture garden at one of his heritage properties. "We had decided to call it Latika Bagh, but she passed away before it could happen," he said.
Article Summary: Sculptor Latika Katt passed away in January last year. The exhibition brings together Abandoned, the last series she created before her passing. A six-minute short film by filmmaker Muzaffar Ali featured Katt and her lifelong inspiration, Varanasi.

Article Title: 'Academics, art can coexist': Mumbai girl hits back at BJP 'Gen Z' post, claims scored 93% in Class 10 and 12
Article Text:
A BJP Chhattisgarh social media post contrasted two Gen Z mindsets using a dancer's video. Urwashi Palandurkar accused the party of using her footage without permission.





MUMBAI: A social media post by the BJP's Chhattisgarh unit contrasting two "Gen Z mindsets" has sparked a political row after Mumbai-based professional dancer and content creator Urwashi Palandurkar, whose protest video was used in the post, accused the party of using her footage without permission and responded with a sarcastic rebuttal that has since gone viral.The BJP Chhattisgarh post asked, "Which mindset Gen Z will you choose?" On one side, it featured a video of Palandurkar with the caption, "Babar ki virasat par thumke lagane wali Gen Z."On the other, it highlighted 14-year-old national judoka Yogita Mandavi, who was recently conferred the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Bal Puraskar by President Droupadi MurmuPalandurkar, who has over 3,00,000 followers on Instagram, first posted the protest dance video during the NEET protest, where it went viral and has since garnered more than 24 million views.Reacting after the BJP post on Instagram, she alleged that her video had been used without her permission. She said the post had led to her direct messages being flooded with people asking if she was okay.Her reaction reel carried the caption: "Please watch till end🙏 I AM NOT OKAY!!!! Not okay with reaching and being followed by the wrong audience 💀 The right ones please engage and help me get my cult balance back🥹🎀."Beginning the video with a serious expression before bursting into laughter, she said, "No, I am not okay. I am that Gen Z student who is facing all this."Calling it her "reaction video", Palandurkar responded point by point to the BJP's post.Mocking the caption, she said, "Your caption game is very weak. Your ChatGPT is not giving you good responses. What is 'Babar ki virasat'? We can't relate with it. Make it more relatable."She also accused the party of trying to divide young people. "Divide and rule in 2026? You're trying to divide the same Gen Z whose unity taught Parliament the term 'Gen Z'. Logic is not logicing," she said.Responding to the comparison between academic excellence and extracurricular activities, Palandurkar said both could coexist. "I got 93% in Class 10 and 93% in Class 12. I danced and created content throughout," she said, showing photographs of medals and certificates displayed at her home.She added that the awards reflected achievements in academics as well as yoga, karate and other activities."Extra-curriculars and academics can coexist, and I am living proof of it," she said.Defending street performances during protests, she added that dancing in public had long been associated with celebration. "I've always seen people dancing on the streets after victories. I don't know why it is not clocking."She also joked about what she called the "brown girl trauma", saying, "Being a brown girl, our parents have already taught us how to deal with trauma. You guys are not able to give trauma. Try harder."Ending the video, Palandurkar acknowledged that she had approached the issue humorously despite its seriousness before signing off with a sarcastic remark, "Vastaguna huiya."The reel has gained traction online and entered the political discourse. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi shared it on his Instagram Story, while Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav posted on X: "Those who are companions on the new path, don't think that they are misguided."The BJP Chhattisgarh unit has not publicly responded to Palandurkar's allegations that her video was used without permission.
Article Summary: BJP's Chhattisgarh unit posted a social media post contrasting two "Gen Z mindsets" Mumbai-based professional dancer Urwashi Palandurkar accused the party of using her footage without permission. She responded with a sarcastic rebuttal that has since gone viral.

Article Title: 4 held for theft of 17 kg silver mask, cladding of Shivling at historic temple in Maharashtra's Khopoli
Article Text:
Khopoli police arrested four burglars for stealing silver items from a historic temple





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khopoli police in Raigad detected the burglary at the 18th century historic Shree Vireshwar temple, where 17 kg silver mask and silver cladding on Shivling was stolen on July 19 past midnight around 2 am, by arresting four accused burglars on Tuesday.The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe (36) and Vikas Agiwale (25), who were arrested from Shirur, Pune district and Dilip Jadhav (40) and Sakharam Gaikwad (40), who were arrested from Parner in Ahilyanagar district.The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust from the donations received from devotees.Sachin Hire, senior inspector of Khopoli said, "On July 19, the assistant priest at the temple identified as Kishore Shigwan (56) lodge a complaint that the silver mask and cladding on Shivling was stolen. The thieves had entered the temple by breaking the chain and lock of the rear gate, which always remained close as the devotees were allowed entry only from the front gate.""Upon checking CCTV camera footage at the temple, it was seen that four masked men had entered the sanctum sanctorum around 2 am and decamped with the silver mask and cladding on the Shivling. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under BNS sections for house tres-pass, theft in a dwelling house and joint criminal liability. "Inspector Hire said, "Multiple teams were formed to trace the gang of burglars.Using technical expertise and informer network, we zeroed-in on four history-sheeters. They were traced to Pune and Ahilyanagar district and gradually apprehended on Tuesday.""They have revealed the place where they have hidden the stolen silver mask and cladding. Accordingly, a police team will recover the stolen valuables. Previously, there are criminal cases of theft and robbery registered against the arrested accused in Ahilyanagar and Pune districts."
Article Summary: The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust. The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe, Vikas Agiwale, Dilip Jadhav and Sakharam Gaikwad.

Article Title: Man booked for sexually assaulting and injuring stray dog in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
Unidentified man booked for sexually assaulting female stray dog (Representative image generated using AI)

It was raining heavily and pitch darkness due to defunct streetlight poles.""I pucker whistled to call the dogs, when a female stray dog, who had delivered puppies last month, came out from behind a plastic table kept horizontally lying on the floor outside the closed tea shop next to the building's main gate. I could see a man hiding behind the table. I became suspicious and asked him what he was doing.""The man ran away semi-naked with his trouser and underwear in his hand.I chased him but taking advantage of the darkness amid heavy rains, he escaped towards the highway."She added, "I called my father downstairs after informing about the incident. I fed the dog and contacted a volunteer of an NGO Jeevan Foundation Yuva Sena, Animal Welfare Force in Kharghar.""I arranged a cab for the volunteer, who took the injured dog to Panvel Panchayat Samiti's Animal Husbandry department, opposite Panvel ST bus depot, where the government veterinarian confirmed sexual assault on the dog, who was treated for the injuries. Article Title: Truck driver arrested from Gujarat for killing fellow driver with iron rod over caste dispute in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Taloja police have caught a truck driver involved in the tragic murder of a fellow driver during a dispute fueled by caste discrimination (Representative image)

NAVI MUMBAI: Taloja police have arrested a 40-year-old truck driver who had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod in the truck parking lot of Nisha Transport company in Nitlas village near Taloja industrial area in Panvel taluka on July 14 early morning.The accused was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday, while he was escaping by train to his home town in UP.The arrested accused has been identified as Ramesh Kumar Yadav and the murder victim as Chandan Pandey, both hailing from UP.Sagar Nikam, PI (crime) of Taloja said, "The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP. The accused Yadav had fatally assaulted the victim Pandey as the latter being a Brahmin used to humiliate Yadav from OBC by treating him as inferior, as claimed by the accused Yadav."PI Nikam informed, "On Monday night, an argument has ensued between Pandey and Yadav in the parking lot over caste discrimination. As they quarrelled, the other truck drivers intervened and resolved the matter. On Tuesday around 5.30 am, again both of them quarrelled, when Yadav assaulted on Pandey's head with an iron rod that proved fatal.""Pandey escaped after threatening other truckers if they attempted to catch him. The security guard Mohammad Alam Hajif-ul Khan (58) informed the police. Pandey was rushed to Panvel sub-district hospital where he was declared brought dead. Subsequently, a murder case was registered against the accused Yadav. His photograph found in his parked truck was immediately circulated to the GRP and RPF at railway stations where multiple trains heading to UP halt.""On Friday, the Valsad GRP informed us that Yadav has been detained at Valsad railway station while he was travelling in an express train to escape to his hometown in UP. Our police team reached Valsad and arrested Yadav. The Panvel JMFC court has remanded Yadav to police custody untill July 21."
Article Summary: Ramesh Kumar Yadav, 40, was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday. He had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod. The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP.

Article Title: BJMC student missing for 13 days, family alleges ragging & harassment
Article Text:
On July 18, the first year MBBS student told a friend he was going to visit a relative in Hadapsar, and has been missing since then

Pune:





Parents of a first year MBBS student of BJ Medical College missing for 13 days have alleged that their son’s batchmates had been harassing and ragging him, even as the college denied the allegations after investigations. The police are also looking for the student after his father lodged an FIR.The student from Kolhapur went missing on July 18.
